hook: A pottery sells every mug it makes for \$20; one small shop cannot change the market price. It could make three mugs a day, or seven. Making more brings in more revenue, but each extra mug also costs more to make. The best output is found one mug at a time: keep going while the next mug adds more to revenue than to cost.

options: the change in total cost divided by the change in output

prereq.q: When economic profit is zero, the firm earns
options: a profit above its opportunity costs
prereq.why: Zero economic profit is normal profit.

prereq.q: A rational decision maker keeps doing more of an activity while
options: its marginal benefit is at least its marginal cost

figure.caption: The firm sells every unit at P, so d = MR = P is a horizontal line. It produces q*, where MR = MC; profit is the rectangle from P down to ATC, out to q*.

chain.cause: Marginal revenue is greater than marginal cost for the next unit
chain.effect: producing it adds MR - MC to profit, so the firm expands

chain.cause: Output rises and diminishing marginal returns push MC up
chain.effect: the gap between MR and MC shrinks
one more unit would add nothing to profit, so profit is at its largest

chain.cause: The firm knows its profit-maximizing output q*
chain.effect: it measures profit as (P - ATC) x q*, the rectangle from the price down to ATC

ideas: Marginal revenue: $\text{MR} = \frac{\Delta \text{TR}}{\Delta Q}$, the extra revenue from one more unit.
The profit-maximizing rule: produce where MR = MC. From a table: the last unit whose MR is at least its MC.
A firm that sells every unit at one market price has MR = AR = P: its demand curve is horizontal, d = MR = AR = P.
Profit = TR - TC = (P - ATC) x q, at the profit-maximizing q: the rectangle between the price and ATC.

misconception.wrong: A firm maximizes profit by producing where its average total cost is lowest, because each unit is cheapest there.
misconception.right: Profit depends on revenue too. The firm produces where MR = MC; that output is at the lowest point of ATC only when the price happens to equal that lowest cost.

summary: Marginal revenue is the change in total revenue from one more unit. A firm maximizes profit by producing where MR = MC: from a table, the last unit whose MR is at least its MC. A firm that sells every unit at a market price it cannot change has MR = AR = P, so its demand curve is a horizontal line, d = MR = AR = P. Profit is TR - TC = (P - ATC) x q at the profit-maximizing output: on a graph, the rectangle from the price down to ATC, out to that output.
